data.answer: Restores are tested every quarter. The most recent restore test was on 12 September 2026 and was completed in 2 hours 40 minutes, within the 4-hour RTO.
Nimbus Labs uses 9 sub-processors that may process customer data. The current list is shared with customers on request. Customers receive 30 days' advance notice before a new sub-processor is added.
Tier 1 vendors are reviewed once a year, and Tier 2 vendors are reviewed every two years. Any vendor that suffers a security incident is reviewed immediately.
A background check covering identity, employment history, and education is completed before the start date for every employee, intern, and contractor.
All access is revoked within 4 hours of the person's exit time.

Customer data is stored in India by default (AWS Mumbai), but disaster recovery copies are held in Singapore. Customers who need all copies kept in India should discuss this with Nimbus Labs before signing.

The provided chunks only detail notification commitments for a *confirmed* breach involving customer data (within 72 hours) and reportable cyber incidents to CERT-In (within 6 hours). They do not address notification for a suspected, unconfirmed security incident.
The provided knowledge chunks do not mention encryption of data while it is in use (such as confidential computing); they only cover encryption at rest and field-level encryption.

The provided chunks outline incident acknowledgement response-time SLAs by severity level (P1: 15 minutes, P2: 1 hour, P3: 1 business day, P4: 3 business days) and customer breach notification within 72 hours, but do not state general contractual support hours.
